Yet so it is with you, if you had hearts to understand it. When you run into sin, run from godliness and refuse to turn at the call of God, you do more against your own souls than men or devils could do otherwise. And if you set yourselves and bent your wits to do yourselves the greatest harm, you could not think of a greater.

4. You are false to the trust God has placed in you. He has entrusted you with much of your own salvation; and will you betray your trust? He has set you to keep your hearts with all diligence; and is this keeping them? (Prov. 4:23).

5. You actually forbid everyone else to pity you when you will have no pity on yourselves.—If you cry to God in the day of your disaster for mercy, mercy, what can you expect but that he will push you away and say, “No, you would not have mercy on yourself. Who brought this on you but your own wilfulness?” And if your fellow men see you in everlasting misery, how will they pity you, when you were your own destroyers and would not be dissuaded?

6. It will make you your own tormentors in hell for ever to think that you brought yourselves wilfully to that misery. Oh, what a torturing thought it will be for ever to think to yourselves that this was your own doing!—That you were warned of this day, and warned again, but it would not do! That you sinned wilfully and wilfully turned away from God! That you had time as well as others, but abused it! That you had teachers as well as others, but refused their instruction! You had holy examples, but did not imitate them. You were offered Christ and grace and glory as well as others, but you had more interest in your fleshly pleasure. You had a price in your hands, but had no heart to spend it (Prov. 17:16).—How can it help but torment you to think of this present folly of yours? Oh, that your eyes were open to see what you have done in wilfully wronging your own souls! And that you understood better these words of God (Prov. 8:33, 34, 35, 36): “Hear instruction, and be wise, and refuse it not. Blessed is the man that heareth me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors. For whoso findeth me findeth life, and shall obtain favour of the Lord. But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul: all they that hate me love death.”

And now that I have come to the end of this work, my heart is troubled to think how I will leave you, in case, after this, the flesh still deceives you, the world and the devil keep you asleep, and I leave you as I found you until you wake up in hell. Though I am afraid of this, out of care for your poor souls and knowing the stubbornness of a carnal heart, yet I can say with the prophet Jeremiah (17:16), “Neither have I desired the woeful day; thou knowest.” I have not, like James and John, wanted “fire to come down from heaven” to consume those who refused Jesus Christ (Luke 9:54); it is preventing the eternal fire that I have been working at all this while! And oh, that it had been unnecessary work! That God and conscience had been as willing to spare me this labour as some of you would have been!—Dear friends! I am so unwilling for you to die in everlasting fire and be shut out of heaven, if it is possible to prevent it, that I will ask you once more: what do you now resolve? Will you turn, or die? I look on you as a physician looks on a patient in a dangerous illness, saying to him, “Though you are far gone, only take this medicine and avoid these few things that are harmful to you, and I will vouch for your life; but if you will not do this, you are a dead man.”—What would you think of such a man, if the physician and all the friends he has could not persuade him to take one medicine to save his life, or to avoid one or two poisonous things that would kill him?—This is your case. However far you have gone in sin, only turn now and come to Christ, take his remedies, and your souls will live. Bring up your deadly sins by repentance, and do not return to the poisonous vomit any more, and you will do well. And yet, if it were your bodies we had to deal with, we might partly know what to do for you. Even if you would not consent, you could be held or tied down while the medicine was poured down your throats, and harmful things could be kept from you. But it cannot be so with your souls; we cannot convert you against your wills. There is no carrying madmen to heaven in chains. You may be condemned against your wills, because you sinned with your wills; but you cannot be saved against your wills. The wisdom of God has seen fit to make people’s salvation or destruction depend very greatly on the choice of their own wills, so that no one will come to heaven who did not choose the way to heaven, and no one will come to hell without being forced to say, “I have what I chose; my own will brought me here.”—Now, if I could only get you to be willing, thoroughly, resolutely and lastingly willing, the work would be more than half done.—And alas! Must we lose our friends, and must they lose their God, their happiness and their souls, for lack of this? Oh, God forbid! It is a strange thing to me that people who are very polite, courteous and good neighbours in lesser matters are so inhuman and stupid in the greatest. For all I know, I have the goodwill of all, or almost all, my neighbours, to the point that if I sent to anyone in the town or parish or county and asked a reasonable favour, they would grant it. And yet when I come to ask them for the greatest thing in the world, for themselves and not for me, I can get nothing from many of them but a patient hearing. I do not know whether people think a man in the pulpit is in earnest or not, and means what he says. For I think I have few neighbours who, if I were sitting with them at home and telling them what I had seen or done or known in the world, would not believe me and heed what I said. But when I tell them, from the infallible word of God, what they themselves will see and know in the world to come, they show by their lives that they either do not believe it or do not much heed it. If I met any one of them on the road and told them, There is a coal pit over there, or a quicksand, or thieves lying in wait for you, I could persuade them to turn aside. But when I tell them that Satan is lying in wait for them, that sin is poison to them, and that hell is not a matter to joke about, they go on as if they did not hear me.—Truly, neighbours, I am as much in earnest with you in the pulpit as I am in any conversation at home; and if you will ever heed me, I beg you, let it be here. I think there is not one of you who, if my own soul depended on your wills, would not be willing to save it (though I cannot promise you would leave your sins for it). If I came hungry or naked to one of your doors, would you not part with more than a cup of drink to relieve me? I am confident you would. If it were to save my life, I know some of you would risk your own. And yet will you not be persuaded to part with your sensual pleasures for your own salvation? I declare to you, Sirs, I am as heartfelt a beggar with you today for the saving of your own souls as I would be for my own needs if I were forced to come begging to your doors. So if you would listen to me then, listen to me now; if you would pity me then, be persuaded now to pity yourselves. I beg you once more, as if I were on my bended knees, to listen to your Redeemer and turn, that you may live.—All you who have lived in ignorance, carelessness and presumption to this day; all you who have been drowned in the cares of the world and have no interest in God and eternal glory; all you who are enslaved to your fleshly desires for food and drink, sports and lusts; and all you who do not know the necessity of holiness and have never known the sanctifying work of the Holy Spirit in your souls; who have never embraced your blessed Redeemer with a living faith and with wondering and thankful thoughts of his love; and who have never felt a higher esteem for God and heaven, and a more heartfelt love for them, than for your fleshly prosperity and the things below: I earnestly beg you, not only for my sake but for the Lord’s sake and for your souls’ sake, not to go one more day in your former condition, but to look around you and cry to God for converting grace, so that you may be made new creatures and may escape the plagues that lie just ahead of you. And if you will ever do anything for me, grant me this request: to turn from your evil ways and live. Deny me anything I ever ask you for myself, if only you will grant me this. And if you deny me this, I do not care about anything else you would grant me. Indeed, as you would ever do anything at the request of the Lord who made you and redeemed you, do not deny him this; for if you deny him this, he cares for nothing else you will grant him. As you would ever have him hear your prayers and grant your requests, and act for you at the hour of death and on the day of judgment, or in any of your extremities, do not deny his request now in the day of your prosperity. Oh, believe me, death and judgment, heaven and hell, are very different things when you come near them from what they seem to carnal eyes from far off.—Well, though I cannot hope so well of all, I will hope that some of you by now intend to turn and live, and are ready to say, “God forbid that we should choose destruction by refusing conversion, as we have done until now.”

If these are the thoughts and intentions of your hearts, I will gladly give you directions on what to do, and briefly, so that you may more easily remember them and put them into practice.

DIRECTION I

IF you want to be converted and saved, work to understand the necessity and true nature of conversion: for what, from what, to what and by what it is that you must turn. Consider what a lamentable condition you are in until the hour of your conversion, so that you may feel it is not a state to rest in. You are under the guilt of all the sins you have ever committed, under the wrath of God and the curse of his law. You are slaves to the devil, employed every day in his work against the Lord, yourselves and others. You are spiritually dead and deformed, being empty of the holy life, nature and image of the Lord. You are unfit for any holy work, and do nothing that is truly pleasing to God. You are without any promise or assurance of his protection, and live in constant danger from his justice, not knowing at what hour you may be snatched away to hell, and quite certain to be damned if you die in that condition. And nothing short of conversion can prevent it. No good manners, improvements or virtues that fall short of true conversion will ever bring about the saving of your souls. Keep a true sense of this natural misery, and so of the necessity of conversion, on your hearts.

And then you must understand what it is to be converted: it is to have a new heart or disposition, and a new way of life.

Question 1. For what must we turn?

Answer. For the following ends, which you may reach. 1. You will immediately be made living members of Christ and have an interest in him; be renewed after the image of God, adorned with all his graces and quickened with a new and heavenly life; be saved from the tyranny of Satan and the dominion of sin; be justified from the curse of the law and have the pardon of all the sins of your whole lives; be accepted by God and made his sons, free to call him Father and to go to him in prayer in all your needs, with a promise of acceptance. You will have the Holy Spirit living in you to sanctify and guide you. You will have a share in the brotherhood, communion and prayers of the saints. You will be fitted for God’s service, freed from the dominion of sin, and be useful and a blessing to the place where you live, and you will have the promise of this life and of the life to come. You will lack nothing that is truly good for you, and you will be enabled to bear your necessary afflictions. You may have some taste of communion with God in the Spirit, especially in all the holy ordinances, where God prepares a feast for your souls. You will be heirs of heaven while you live on earth, and may see the everlasting glory ahead by faith, and so may live and die in peace; and you will never be brought so low that your happiness is not incomparably greater than your misery.—How precious every one of these blessings is, which I only name briefly, and which you may receive in this life!

And then, 2. At death your souls will go to Christ, and on the day of judgment both soul and body will be justified and glorified and enter into your Master’s joy, where your happiness will consist in these particulars:

1. You yourselves will be made perfect.—Your mortal bodies will be made immortal, and the corruptible will put on incorruption. You will no longer be hungry or thirsty or weary or sick, nor will you need to fear shame or sorrow or death or hell. Your souls will be perfectly freed from sin and perfectly fitted for the knowledge, love and praise of the Lord.

2. Your work will be to see your glorious Redeemer, with all your holy fellow citizens of heaven; to see the glory of the most blessed God; to love him perfectly and be loved by him; and to praise him for ever.

3. Your glory will add to the glory of the New Jerusalem, the city of the living God, which is more than having a private happiness for yourselves.

4. Your glory will add to the glorifying of your Redeemer, who will be magnified and pleased for ever in you, who are the travail of his soul; and this is more than the glorifying of yourselves.

5. And the eternal Majesty, the living God, will be glorified in your glory: as he is magnified by your praises, as he shares his glory and goodness with you, and as he is pleased in you and in the completion of his glorious work, in the glory of the New Jerusalem and of his Son. All this the poorest beggar among you who is converted will certainly and endlessly enjoy.

2. You see for what you must turn. Next you must understand from what you must turn. In a word, it is from your carnal self, which is the end of all the unconverted: from the flesh, which wants to be pleased before God and would keep enticing you; from the world, which is the bait; and from the devil, who is the angler for souls and the deceiver; and so from all known and wilful sins.

3. Next you must know to what you must turn: that is, to God as your end; to Christ as the way to the Father; to holiness, as the way Christ has appointed for you; and to the use of all the helps and means of grace the Lord gives you.

4. Lastly, you must know by what you must turn: that is, by Christ, as the only Redeemer and Intercessor; by the Holy Spirit, as the sanctifier; by the Word, as his instrument or means; and by faith and repentance, as the means and duties to be performed on your part. All this is necessary.

Direction II. If you want to be converted and saved, give much time to private, serious thought. Thoughtlessness ruins the world. Withdraw often to a private place, and there think about the purpose for which you were made; the life you have lived; the time you have lost; the sin you have committed; the love and sufferings and fullness of Christ; the danger you are in; the nearness of death and judgment; the certainty and excellence of the joys of heaven; the certainty and terror of the torments of hell, and the eternity of both; and the necessity of conversion and a holy life. Steep your hearts in thoughts like these.

Direction III. If you want to be converted and saved, give attention to the word of God, which is the ordinary means. Read the Scripture, or hear it read, and other holy writings that apply it. Attend the public preaching of the word faithfully. Just as God will light the world by the sun, and not by himself alone without it, so he will convert and save people by his ministers, who are the lights of the world (Acts 26:17, 18; Matt. 5:14). When he had miraculously humbled Paul, he sent him to Ananias (Acts 9:10). And when he sent an angel to Cornelius, it was only to tell him to send for Peter, who was to tell him what to believe and do.

Direction IV. “Give yourselves to God in a course of earnest, constant prayer. Confess and lament your former lives, and beg his grace to enlighten and convert you. Plead with him to pardon what is past, to give you his Spirit, to change your hearts and lives, to lead you in his ways, and to save you from temptations.” Keep at this work daily, and do not grow weary of it.

Direction V. “Give up your known and wilful sins at once. Stop, and go no further that way.”—Do not get drunk any more, but avoid the place and the occasion of it. Throw away your lusts and sinful pleasures with loathing, and do not rail any more; and if you have wronged anyone, make restitution as Zacchaeus did. If you will commit your old sins again, what blessing can you expect on the means of conversion?

Direction VI. “At once, if possible, change your company, if it has been bad until now.” Do this not by abandoning your necessary relationships, but your unnecessary, sinful companions; and join yourselves to those who fear the Lord, and ask them the way to heaven (Acts 9:19, 26; Psa. 15:4).

Direction VII. “Give yourselves up to the Lord Jesus as the physician of your souls,” so that he may pardon you by his blood and sanctify you by his Spirit, and by his word and ministers, the instruments of the Spirit. He is the way, the truth and the life; there is no coming to the Father except by him (John 14:6). “Neither is there any other name under heaven by which you can be saved” (Acts 4:12). So study his person and nature, what he has done and suffered for you, what he is to you and what he will be, and how he is fitted to supply all your needs in full.

Direction VIII. If you really mean to turn and live, “do it quickly, without delay.” If you are not willing to turn today, you are not willing to do it at all.—Remember that all this while you are in your blood, under the guilt of many thousands of sins and under God’s wrath, and you stand at the very brink of hell; there is only a step between you and death. And this is not a situation for anyone in his right mind to be at ease in. So get up at once and flee as for your lives, as you would get out of your house if it were all on fire over your heads.—Oh, if only you knew the constant danger you live in, the unspeakable loss you suffer every day, and what a safer and sweeter life you could live, you would not stand trifling but would turn at once. Multitudes are lost who wilfully delay when they are convinced that it must be done. Your lives are short and uncertain; and what a state you are in if you die before you have thoroughly turned! You have waited too long already and wronged God too long. Sin gains strength and puts down roots while you delay. Your conversion will become harder and more doubtful. You have much to do, so do not put it all off to the end, in case God abandons you and gives you up to yourselves, and then you are ruined for ever.

Direction IX. If you will turn and live, do it “without reservation, absolutely and universally.” Do not think to bargain with Christ, divide your heart between him and the world, part with some sins and keep the rest, and let go only what your flesh can spare. This is only self-deception. In heart and resolve you must forsake all you have, or else you cannot be his disciples (Luke 14:26, 33). If you will not take God and heaven for your portion and lay everything below at the feet of Christ, but must also have your good things here and an earthly portion, as if God and glory were not enough for you, it is useless to dream of salvation on these terms, for it will not happen. However religious you may seem, if it is still only a carnal righteousness, and the flesh’s prosperity or pleasure or safety is still held back from your devotion to God, this is as certain a road to death as open profanity, though it may look more respectable.

Direction X. If you will turn and live, do it “resolutely,” and do not stand still deliberating as if it were a doubtful case. Do not stand wavering, as if you were still unsure whether God or the flesh is the better master, whether heaven or hell is the better end, or whether sin or holiness is the better way. Away with your former lusts, and resolve at once, lastingly and firmly. Do not be of one mind one day and of another the next; settle the matter with all the world, and resolutely give up yourselves and all you have to God. Now, while you are reading or hearing this, resolve. Before you sleep another night, resolve. Before you move from this place, resolve. Before Satan has time to draw you off, resolve. You never really turn until you resolve, and that with a firm, unchangeable resolve.—So much for the Directions.

And now I have done my part in this work, so that you may turn at the call of God and live. What will come of it I cannot tell. I have sown the seed at God’s command, but it is not in my power to give the increase. I can go no further with my message. I cannot bring it into your hearts or make it work. I cannot do your part for you in receiving it and considering it. I cannot do God’s part by opening your hearts to make you receive it. Nor can I show heaven or hell to your eyes, or give you new and tender hearts. If I knew what more to do for your conversion, I hope I would do it.

But O you who are the gracious Father of spirits, you have sworn that you do not delight in the death of the wicked, but rather that they turn and live. Do not deny your blessing to these persuasions and directions, and do not let your enemies triumph in your sight, or the great deceiver of souls prevail against your Son, your Spirit and your Word! Oh, pity poor unconverted sinners, who have no heart to pity themselves. Command the blind to see, the deaf to hear and the dead to live, and do not let sin and death be able to resist you.—Awaken the complacent, settle the unresolved, strengthen the wavering, and let the eyes of sinners who read these lines next be used in weeping over their sins. Bring them to themselves and to your Son before their sins have brought them to ruin. If you only say the word, these poor efforts will prosper in winning many a soul, to their everlasting joy and everlasting glory. Amen.

THE END.
